_doc: Opcode table for the iCAN CX68 = CamelTech CT-M68, device id 2427, model ry5088_cx68bug_8k_002_dm. Effective FEA_CMD_* constants of its protocol class chain wGa -> Kka -> kba -> Uga -> YHe -> EG -> lG -> JC -> RC -> AC in iotdriver.qmk.top's bundle (regenerate with tools/capture/class_chain.py). Byte 0 of the 64-byte feature report (interface 2, report ID 0). kind: read = GET, write = changes config, volatile = runtime state only. Anything not listed here, or listed under deny, is never sent.
class_chain: wGa Kka kba Uga YHe EG lG JC RC AC

checksum._doc: Bit7: b[7] = 0xFF - (sum(b[0..6]) & 0xFF). Bit8: b[8] = 0xFF - (sum(b[0..7]) & 0xFF). The helper zero-pads to 9 bytes before the checksum, then to 64. In this class chain commands use BIT7 (enum 0) except setLightSetting (0x07: Uga calls writeFeatureCmd(a, 1, 50), and b[7] carries blue), setSLEDParam (0x08) and setOledEffect (0x2B), which use BIT8 (enum 1, proto.driver.CheckSumType = {BIT7: 0, BIT8: 1, NONE: 2}). NONE is only used by the OLED upgrade (denied), so none_opcodes stays empty.

0x03.name: SET_REPORT_RATE
0x03.note: [0x03, profile, rateCode]; RC maps only 1000/500/250/125 Hz; the page never calls it for the CX68 (8 kHz board) - open question

0x07.name: SET_LEDPARAM
0x07.note: [0x07, mode, MAXSPEED(4) - speed, brightness, option (low nibble colour: 8 rainbow, 7 rgb, 0..6 preset; high nibble direction), r, g, b] BIT8 (checksum in b[8]); white is sent as FA FF FA. From Uga.setLightSetting

0x08.name: SET_SIDE_LEDPARAM
0x08.note: [0x08, mode, speed, brightness, option, r, g, b] BIT8, sent with 500 ms delay

0x0A.name: SET_KEYMATRIX
0x0A.note: bulk: [0x0A, profile, 0xFF, page, len, last, ...] + 56 data bytes (4 bytes per key); single: [0x0A, profile, keyPos, ..., b[5]=1, b[6]=layer offset, b[8..11]=4-byte code]. In some other RY classes 0x0A is reset; this entry is only valid for this class chain

0x10.name: SET_FN
0x10.note: [0x10, os (0 win, 1 mac), fn layer, slot, 0, 0, 0, ck, 4-byte entry] BIT7. From Uga.setFnKeyConfigSimple

0x1B.name: SET_TRAVEL_REPORT
0x1B.note: [0x1B, 1|0] BIT7; enables/disables travel notifications (interface 1, report 5, first byte 0x1B)

0x1D.name: SET_KEY_MAGNETISM_MODE
0x1D.note: [0x1D, mode (0 comfort,1 sensitive,2 gaming,3 custom), keyboardDisable, gamepadEnable]; the page sends 1D 03 00 00 on opening key settings

0x65.name: SET_MAGNETISM_BY_ARR
0x65.note: [0x65, param, bulk(1)/single(0), page, last, ...]; BIT7; data 56 bytes per packet; values as for 0xE5

0x89.name: GET_KBOPTION
0x89.note: [0x89, profile]; reply flags at b[2], options b[3], b[4]

0x8A.name: GET_KEYMATRIX
0x8A.note: [0x8A, profile, 0xFF, page 0..7, layer]; reply is raw 4-byte entries, no opcode echo

0x8F.name: GET_REV
0x8F.note: reply: u32 LE device id at [1..4] (2427), firmware version (b[8]<<8)|b[7] (0x0400)

0x9D.name: GET_KEY_MAGNETISM_MODE
0x9D.note: [0x9D]; reply [0x9D, mode, keyboardDisable, gamepadEnable] - reads gamepad state without writing

0xE5.name: GET_MAGNETISM_BY_ARR
0xE5.note: [0xE5, param, bulk=1, page]; reply = raw values, no opcode echo. u16 LE per matrix slot, 32 per page, 4 pages = 128 slots, units 0.01 mm (firmware 0x0400). params: 0 actuation, 1 release ('lift'), 2 RT press, 3 RT release, 4 DKS start, 5 MT hold time, 6 bottom deadzone, 7 key mode byte (u8, 2 pages), 8 DKS flags, 9 snap/SOCD partner, 10 all-keys DKS flags, 252 switch type, 254 live press travel, 255 live dynamic value. Factory defaults: actuation 200, release 280, deadzone 30, RT 50/50

deny.0x00: SET_REV (purpose not documented). Also what setKeyMagnetismFast actually sends on this class chain: FEA_CMD_SET_MAGNETISM_FAST is undefined here, so byte 0 stays 0x00 - a vendor bug
deny.0x02: SET_BATTERY_LP (wireless low-power; unused on this wired board) / factory reset in older RY classes
deny.0xBA: firmware upgrade start/verify (BA C0 / BA C2)
deny.0x1C: write min-travel calibration (only inside an explicit, user-confirmed calibration flow)
deny.0x1E: write max-travel calibration (only inside an explicit, user-confirmed calibration flow)

deny_rules: any opcode not listed in commands (unknown purpose)
any packet whose checksum does not match its opcode's checksum type (Bit7 by default; NONE only for none_opcodes)
WebHID output reports, and the helper's sendRawFeature/readRawFeature/cleanDev/upgradeOTAGATT
